work.permit: permit granted by the Minister of Labour under Sectoral Determination 10

note: Read 2026-10-31 on gov.za (the Government Communication and Information System's document library). Majority: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s. 17: a child, male or female, becomes a major at eighteen. Work: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997, s. 43(1) (as gov.za publishes it; later amendments not traced): no one may employ a child under fifteen, or under the minimum school-leaving age if that is fifteen or older (the end of grade 9 or fifteen, under the South African Schools Act, not read); s. 43(2): no child in work inappropriate to the age or risking well-being or schooling; children of fifteen to seventeen are further limited by the hazardous-work regulations (not held). Performers: Sectoral Determination 10, Children in the performance of advertising, artistic and cultural activities (GN R. 882, Government Gazette 26608, 29 July 2004), clause 2: from 16 August 2004 no person may employ a child under fifteen in advertising, artistic and cultural activities except under a permit granted under the Determination; applications go to the Minister of Labour on Form SD 10.1, the permit issues on Form SD 10.2, and sets its period and conditions; no lowest age (the Determination sets hours by age band, ten and under, under five, not held). An amending notice to the Determination (its form SD 10.1) was saved but not otherwise read. Service: Service is held null: no source saying no service is asked was reached today (the blocker file names the attempts); a reading only, not held: the South African National Defence Force recruits volunteers and no law asks military service (no source saved).
